value.rationale: The complete distribution at a fixed sample depth is an observable sufficient-statistic candidate in idealized taxon sampling. A sharp first obstruction at n=10 and a complete list of minimal two-depth designs distinguish possible exact sampling schemes, and require a genuinely exhaustive and nontrivial shape comparison; unlike arbitrary tabulations, this gives a motivated sampling identifiability boundary. Restricted unit edge lengths, unlabeled topology, noiseless population histograms and n<=10 are explicitly stated.
